q: who is the main character of hamlet
a: Hamlet is a tragedy by William Shakespeare, written around 1599-1601, widely considered one of the greatest plays in the English language. The plot: Prince Hamlet of Denmark returns from university to find that his father, King Hamlet, has died and his mother Gertrude has quickly married his uncle Claudius, who has taken the throne. The ghost of the old king appears and reveals that Claudius murdered him, demanding revenge. Hamlet feigns madness to investigate, but his indecision — famously captured in the 'To be, or not to be' soliloquy — drives the tragedy: he accidentally kills Polonius, which leads to Ophelia's madness and drowning; Claudius sends him to England with a death warrant he escapes; and the play ends in a bloody duel in which Claudius, Gertrude, Laertes, and Hamlet himself all die. Its themes of revenge, mortality, madness, and corruption have made it endlessly analyzed and performed.

the theme of the great gatsby
a: The Great Gatsby (1925) is a novel by American author F. Scott Fitzgerald, set in the summer of 1922 in the fictional towns of West Egg and East Egg on Long Island, New York, with frequent excursions to Manhattan. It is narrated by Nick Carraway, who observes his mysterious millionaire neighbor Jay Gatsby's obsessive pursuit of Daisy Buchanan, a woman Gatsby loved before the war and who has since married the wealthy, brutish Tom Buchanan. Gatsby's lavish parties are all staged to attract Daisy, and their reunion sets off a chain of tragedy ending in Gatsby's death, unmourned by the 'careless people' who used him. The novel's central message is a critique of the American Dream: Gatsby's wealth cannot buy Daisy or erase his past, and the Jazz Age's glittering surface conceals moral emptiness, class rigidity, and corruption. Its final line — 'So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past' — has become iconic.

q: who is the villain of star wars
who is the main villain of star wars
a: The central villain of the original Star Wars trilogy is Darth Vader, a Sith Lord in black armor who serves Emperor Palpatine (Darth Sidious), the true mastermind of the Galactic Empire. Vader, born Anakin Skywalker, was once a promising Jedi who fell to the dark side in the prequel trilogy after being seduced by promises of power to save his wife Padmé, and was horrifically burned in a duel with his mentor Obi-Wan Kenobi, requiring his iconic mechanical suit and breathing apparatus. The Empire is also served by Grand Moff Tarkin, who orders the destruction of Alderaan. Later films add Kylo Ren (Ben Solo), Vader's grandson, as the primary antagonist of the sequel trilogy. Vader's arc ends with redemption: in Return of the Jedi (1983), he throws Palpatine to his death to save his son Luke, fulfilling the prophecy of the Chosen One.

q: who is the main character of hamlet
a: The main character of Hamlet is Prince Hamlet of Denmark, the title character of Shakespeare's tragedy. He is the son of the murdered King Hamlet and Queen Gertrude, and nephew of his stepfather, King Claudius. Hamlet is one of literature's most complex protagonists: a scholar and wit who is plunged into grief and tasked with avenging his father's murder, he feigns madness, contemplates suicide in his famous 'To be, or not to be' soliloquy, and ultimately fulfills his revenge at the cost of his own life and those of nearly everyone around him. His character — melancholic, intellectual, and paralyzed by overthinking — has generated centuries of debate, with critics split on whether he is a heroic avenger or a man undone by his own indecision. The role is considered one of the most demanding in the acting canon.
